title: Soldier Blade
subtitle: Seven operations at full speed
summary: Soldier Blade is Hudson's vertically scrolling shooter, first released for PC Engine on 10 July 1992.
body: Soldier Blade is Hudson's vertically scrolling shooter, first released for PC Engine on 10 July 1992. The player's spacecraft crosses seven operations against the invading Zeograd Army, moving between formations, large enemies and bosses. Colored capsules provide different weapons, allowing the ship's fire to change as the action advances. Its emphasis on speed makes each approaching pattern a quick decision about position and firepower, while the clear weapon system lets the player read the consequences of collecting the next capsule immediately.

The available weapons include a spreading Vulcan shot, a wave gun and a laser. Power-ups also bring a supporting pod, and up to three items can be stored for later use. Spending a weapon unleashes a powerful special attack, making the reserve a way to respond when the screen becomes dangerous. Taking damage can reduce the ship's strength, so collecting and preserving power remains part of the challenge. Bosses and intermediate encounters interrupt the scrolling stages with larger targets whose weak points must be reached through the surrounding fire.

The project grew from planning for Hudson's Caravan tournament, and two-minute and five-minute score modes sit beside the main campaign. They condense the shooting into a repeatable contest over a fixed span of time. Designer Uriko Uribo worked under a short production schedule, while Keita Hoshi and Makiko Tanifuji composed the soundtrack. Yuji Kaida created the cover illustration. The finished game connects a full seven-stage journey with the tournament tradition of learning a short sequence closely enough to improve its score on the next attempt.
story_headings: A shooter built for the Caravan
